title: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

blocks.tex: In statements quoted from \cite{LWX126}, spectra are assumed to be $2$-completed, connective and of finite type. Write $E_2^{s,t}$ for the mod-two Adams $E_2$-page, with stem $t-s$. This chapter records the specified Ext generators, bases, products and their comparisons with the sphere and cofiber pages. The bounded sphere comparison is defined for $t\leq261$. These algebraic inputs precede the proof tools; later Adams differentials and survival calculations appear in Chapter~6.

A generator catalogue records every generator and its degree; a source monomial is formed from its unit, generators and degree-preserving products.

blocks.label: sem:Computation:source-presentation
blocks.title: The source presentation and complete archive
blocks.body: A source presentation consists of bigraded $\mathbb F_2$-modules, specified bilinear products, a unit element and the named atoms. A sphere archive specifies its complete generator list, the exact identification of every atom, and every basis monomial in each bidegree. Evaluation of a monomial uses these same products and generator values.

blocks.label: sem:Computation:source-basis
blocks.title: Complete source coordinates
blocks.body:
For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and $t\leq261$, the source coordinates are a linear equivalence
\[P^{s,t}\cong\bigoplus_{i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)}\mathbb F_2.\]
The inverse of each coordinate unit vector is the value of the corresponding archived monomial. In particular, the archived monomials form a basis of $P^{s,t}$.

      (archive.basisMonomial s t i).value sourceData sourceGenerator := by sorry

blocks.label: sem:Computation:bounded-comparison
blocks.title: The bounded comparison
blocks.body: For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and $t\leq261$, the fixed comparison is a linear equivalence from $P^{s,t}$ to the actual sphere $E_2^{s,t}$. A sphere presentation requires the comparison to preserve the specified unit and every product of total degree $t+t\prime\leq261$, and to identify the selected $h_i$ with the fixed standard classes.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.SpherePresentation
lean.code:
public structure SpherePresentation (D : Model C Syn) (P : ProgramData.{v}) where
  comparison : ∀ s t : ℕ, t ≤ 261 →
    P.component s t ≃ₗ[ℤ] D.classical.sphere.Page 2 ((s : ℤ),(t : ℤ))
  comparison_product : ∀ s t s' t' : ℕ, ∀ h : t+t' ≤ 261,
    ∀ (x : P.component s t) (y : P.component s' t'),
    comparison (s+s') (t+t') h (P.product s t s' t' x y) =
      D.sphereAlgebra.product (s,t) (s',t')
        (comparison s t (by omega) x) (comparison s' t' (by omega) y)
  comparison_unit : comparison 0 0 (by decide) P.unit = D.sphereAlgebra.unit
  h0 : comparison 1 1 (by decide) (P.atom .h0) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 0
  h1 : comparison 1 2 (by decide) (P.atom .h1) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 1
  h2 : comparison 1 4 (by decide) (P.atom .h2) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 2
  h4 : comparison 1 16 (by decide) (P.atom .h4) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 4
  h5 : comparison 1 32 (by decide) (P.atom .h5) = D.standardClasses.standardHi 5
  h6 : comparison 1 64 (by decide) (P.atom .h6) = D.standardClasses.standardH6

The comparison is $\mathbb F_2$-linear.

blocks.label: sem:Computation:actual-coordinates
blocks.title: Coordinates on the actual page
blocks.body:
For $t\leq261$, composition of the inverse comparison with the source coordinates gives
\[E_2^{s,t}\cong\bigoplus_{i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)}\mathbb F_2.\]
Its inverse sends each unit vector to the image of the same archived monomial. Pulling that vector back by the comparison recovers the original source monomial.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.SpherePresentation.coordinates_basis
lean.code:
public theorem coordinates_basis (e : SpherePresentation D P)
    (S : SourceBasisSpecification P A) (s t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ 261)
    (i : Fin (A.basisCount s t)) :
    (e.coordinates S s t ht).symm (Finsupp.single i 1) =
      e.comparison s t ht ((A.basisMonomial s t i).value P S.generator) := by
  change e.comparison s t ht ((S.coordinates s t ht).symm (Finsupp.single i 1)) = _
  rw [S.basis_values]
lean.statement:

    (i : Fin (A.basisCount s t)) :

Every actual coordinate unit vector is the image of the same archived
monomial, not a freshly selected basis of the same dimension.

blocks.label: sem:Computation:top-cell-comparison
blocks.title: Identification of the top-cell image
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived nu-cofiber comparison.)\par
The image of $a$ under the actual cofiber connecting arrow desuspends, through the prescribed four sphere suspensions and shift coherence maps, to $X=h_1x_{121,7}$. The comparison supplies the intermediate labels in degrees $(8,133)$, $(8,132)$ and $(8,131)$.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.Standard.top_comparison
lean.code:
public theorem top_comparison :
  ∃ (a3 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 3)).Page 2 (8,133))
    (a2 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 2)).Page 2 (8,132))
    (a1 : (model.classical.obj (Sphere 1)).Page 2 (8,131)),
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 3 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 134
      (model.classical.pageMap (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibδ model.auxiliary.nuMap) 2 (8,134) topCell) a3 ∧
    (model.classicalSuspension (.shift 2 .sphere)).DesuspendsClass 8 133
      (model.classical.pageMap
        ((shiftFunctorAdd' Spectrum (2 : ℤ) 1 3 (by decide)).hom.app SphereSpectrum)
        2 (8,133) a3) a2 ∧

blocks.label: sem:Computation:table-coordinate-syntax
blocks.title: Finite table coordinates
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived finite tables.)\par
A table row specifies the sphere or $C\nu$, an Adams bidegree and an increasing list of coordinate indices. A row is coordinate-valid if its degree occurs in the table and its coordinate indices are strictly increasing and less than the tabulated dimension.

blocks.label: sem:Computation:table-realization
blocks.title: Realization and decoding of a table row
blocks.body:
For $o=S^0$ or $C\nu$, write $b_{o;s,t,i}\in E_2^{s,t}(o)$ for the specified basis vectors. For the sphere, $t\leq261$ and $i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)$, these are the inverse coordinate images of the unit vectors; set $b_{S^0;s,t,i}=0$ when either bound fails. A coordinate-valid list $I$ represents
\[\sum_{i\in I}b_{o;s,t,i}.\]
An invalid coordinate list represents no element. The basis is complete if there is a linear coordinate equivalence sending every $b_{o;s,t,i}$ to the corresponding unit vector.

lean.name: KIP126.Computation.Table.basis_correct
lean.code:
public theorem basis_correct (d : Raw.Degree) (hd : d ∈ Raw.degrees) : BasisCorrect d := by
  rcases d with ⟨o,s,t,ms⟩
  cases o with
  | sphere =>
    have hc := basis_count ⟨.sphere,s,t,ms⟩ hd rfl
    have ht := table_degree_bound ⟨.sphere,s,t,ms⟩ hd
    dsimp only at hc ht
    change ∃ e : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t) ≃ₗ[ℤ] (Fin ms.length →₀ ZMod 2),
      ∀ i, e.symm (Finsupp.single i 1) = sphereBasis s t i.val
    rw [← hc]
    refine ⟨Standard.coordinates s t ht, ?_⟩
    intro i
    simp only [sphereBasis, dif_pos ht, dif_pos i.isLt]

lean.code:
public theorem basis_count (d : Raw.Degree) (hd : d ∈ Raw.degrees)
    (hs : d.spectrum = .sphere) :
    Standard.archive.basisCount d.s d.t = d.monomials.length := by
  have hbound : ∀ d ∈ Raw.degrees, d.t ≤ 261 := by decide
  rw [archive_dimension d.s d.t (hbound d hd)]
  have hlength : ∀ d ∈ Raw.degrees, d.spectrum = .sphere →
      basisDimension d.s d.t = d.monomials.length := by decide
  exact hlength d hd hs

blocks.label: sem:Computation:polynomial-values
blocks.title: Polynomial expressions and calibrated basis values
blocks.body: Let $G_{j;s,t}$ be the image in $E_2^{s,t}$ of archived generator $j$ when $t\leq261$ and $j$ has bidegree $(s,t)$, and set $G_{j;s,t}=0$ otherwise. Expressions are formed from $1$, the named atoms, the elements $G_{j;s,t}$ and products. Their values are computed in the sphere $E_2$-page. For each basis-value record $(e,i)$, the $i$th basis vector in the bidegree of $e$ equals the value of $e$.

  if ht : t ≤ 261 then
    if hi : id < Standard.archive.generators.count then
      if hd : Standard.archive.generators.degree ⟨id,hi⟩ = (s,t) then
        Standard.comparison s t ht
          ((eqToHom (congrArg (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => Standard.sourceData.component p.1 p.2) hd))
            (Standard.sourceGenerator ⟨id,hi⟩))
      else 0
    else 0
  else 0

blocks.body:
The sphere basis vectors satisfy
\[b_{S^0;11,133,1}=P,\qquad b_{S^0;12,134,0}=Q,\qquad b_{S^0;14,139,1}=T,\]
\[b_{S^0;10,134,4}=U,\qquad b_{S^0;13,137,1}=C,\qquad b_{S^0;13,137,2}=h_4x_{109,12}.\]
If $x\in E_2^{s,t}$, $y\in E_2^{s\prime,t\prime}$ and $t+t\prime\leq261$, then $xy=yx$. Moreover, $h_0h_1=h_1h_2=0$.

blocks.label: sem:E2Computation:two-line-exhaustive
blocks.title: Exhaustive standard products on the Adams second line
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Adams60}, Theorem 2.5.1(2), p.~45.)\par{}

For every integer $t$ and nonzero $x\in E_2^{2,t}(S^0)$, there are natural numbers $i\leq j$ and a bidegree equation
\[
 (1,2^i)+(1,2^j)=(2,t)
\]
such that $x$ equals the corresponding transport of $H_{i,j}$. There is no upper bound on $t$, $i$ or $j$.

lean.name: KIP126.E2Computation.two_line_exhaustive
lean.code:
public theorem two_line_exhaustive (t : ℤ) (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (2,t))
    (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i j : ℕ, i ≤ j ∧
      ∃ degree : hiDegree i + hiDegree j = (2,t),
        x = (eqToHom (congrArg (ActualE2At model.classical) degree))
          (KIP126.Literature.Standard.hiProduct i j) := by
  sorry
lean.statement:
public theorem two_line_exhaustive (t : ℤ) (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (2,t))
    (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i j : ℕ, i ≤ j ∧
      ∃ degree : hiDegree i + hiDegree j = (2,t),
        x = (eqToHom (congrArg (ActualE2At model.classical) degree))
          (KIP126.Literature.Standard.hiProduct i j)
lean.docstring:
Every nonzero homogeneous second-line element is a standard product.
The degree equation and equality are in the actual fixed E₂ module.

comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Original source checked directly: [Adams60](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970147), Theorem 2.5.1(2), pp.~44--45, gives the second-line basis h_j h_i for j>=i>=0 and j!=i+1. [LinExt4](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.topol.2007.11.003), Theorem 1.2, p.~460, recalls this earlier result and is not its original source. Distinct ordered power-of-two pairs have distinct sums, so each nonzero homogeneous element over F2 is a single basis product. The theorem is adapted to integer grading, actual page products and their degree transports. Identification of the abstract Ext basis with the project's fixed E2 product remains the registered E2Computation obligation; this source check does not prove it. The finite archive bound t<=261 is not extrapolated. Primary text: [Adams](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Adams-HI1.pdf), Theorem 2.5.1(2), p.45.

The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $\delta:C\nu\to S^3[1]$ be the cofiber connecting map, and let $\sigma_{j,1}:S^j[1]\cong S^{j+1}$ be the fixed shift-coherence isomorphisms. There are classes
\[a_3\in E_2^{8,133}(S^3),\quad a_2\in E_2^{8,132}(S^2),\quad a_1\in E_2^{8,131}(S^1)\]
such that $\delta_*a$ desuspends to $a_3$, $(\sigma_{2,1}^{-1})_*a_3$ desuspends to $a_2$, $(\sigma_{1,1}^{-1})_*a_2$ desuspends to $a_1$, and $a_1$ desuspends to $X$. These are the four fixed sphere desuspension relations.
\item $Xh_2=0\in E_2^{9,134}(S^0)$.
\end{enumerate}
